    11	/-!
    12	# Standard opens and their localization maps
    13	
    14	The standard open `D(f)` on an affine open is represented on sections by the
    15	localization away from `f`.  This file exposes that fact and the induced map
    16	between such localizations under a ring homomorphism.

    19	namespace StacksPart02

    25	/-- Sections on a standard open of an affine open are the localization away
    26	from the defining section (Stacks, Tag 01HS(1)). -/
    27	theorem affineOpen_standardOpen_isLocalization
    28	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (f : Γ(X, U)) :
    29	    IsLocalization.Away f Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) := by
    30	  exact hU.isLocalization_basicOpen f
    31	
    32	/-- The corresponding statement for an affine scheme and a global section. -/
    33	theorem affineScheme_standardOpen_isLocalization
    34	    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] (f : Γ(X, ⊤)) :
    35	    IsLocalization.Away f Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) := by
    36	  infer_instance

    38	section RingMap
    39	
    40	variable {R S Rf Sf : Type*}
    41	variable [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S]
    42	variable [CommSemiring Rf] [CommSemiring Sf]
    43	variable [Algebra R Rf] [Algebra S Sf]
    44	
    45	/-- The canonical map between localizations induced by a ring map.
    46	
    47	If `Rf` is `R` localized away from `f` and `Sf` is `S` localized away from
    48	`φ(f)`, this is the map supplied by the universal property of localization.
    49	-/
    50	noncomputable def standardOpenLocalizationMap
    51	    (φ : R →+* S) (f : R)
    52	    [IsLocalization.Away f Rf]
    53	    [IsLocalization.Away (φ f) Sf] :
    54	    Rf →+* Sf :=
    55	  IsLocalization.Away.map Rf Sf φ f
    56	
    57	@[simp]
    58	theorem standardOpenLocalizationMap_algebraMap
    59	    (φ : R →+* S) (f : R)
    60	    [IsLocalization.Away f Rf]
    61	    [IsLocalization.Away (φ f) Sf] (a : R) :
    62	    standardOpenLocalizationMap φ f (algebraMap R Rf a) =
    63	      algebraMap S Sf (φ a) := by
    64	  have h : Submonoid.powers f ≤ (Submonoid.powers (φ f)).comap φ := by
    65	    rintro x ⟨n, rfl⟩
    66	    exact ⟨n, by simp⟩
    67	  change IsLocalization.map Sf φ h (algebraMap R Rf a) = algebraMap S Sf (φ a)
    68	  exact IsLocalization.map_eq h a
    69	
    70	/-- Ring-hom form of `standardOpenLocalizationMap_algebraMap`. -/
    71	theorem standardOpenLocalizationMap_comp_algebraMap
    72	    (φ : R →+* S) (f : R)
    73	    [IsLocalization.Away f Rf]
    74	    [IsLocalization.Away (φ f) Sf] :
    75	    (standardOpenLocalizationMap φ f).comp (algebraMap R Rf) =

   160	noncomputable def standardOpenLocalizedModuleMapOfSubset {f g : R}

import StacksPart01Lib.Integral
import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Lifts
import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Prod

/-!
# Integral elements in finite products

The source allows the component maps to have different base rings.  The
surjective-base helper below supplies the coefficient-lifting step needed to
reduce that statement to Mathlib's product-algebra theorem.
-/

namespace StacksPart01

open Polynomial

/-! A monic witness can be lifted across a surjective base map. -/

theorem integralElem_comp_surjective_iff
    {R R' S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [Ring S]
    (g : R →+* R') (hg : Function.Surjective g) (f : R' →+* S) {x : S} :
    (f.comp g).IsIntegralElem x ↔ f.IsIntegralElem x := by
  constructor
  · exact RingHom.IsIntegralElem.of_comp
  · rintro ⟨p, hp, hx⟩
    obtain ⟨q, hq, _, hqm⟩ :=
      Polynomial.lifts_and_natDegree_eq_and_monic
        (Polynomial.mem_lifts_of_surjective hg p) hp
    refine ⟨q, hqm, ?_⟩
    rw [← Polynomial.eval₂_map g f x, hq]
    exact hx

/-! [Stacks tag 0CY8] -/

/-- For componentwise ring maps, integrality in a binary product is
equivalent to integrality in each component. -/
theorem isIntegralElem_prodMap_iff
    {R₁ R₂ S₁ S₂ : Type*}
    [CommRing R₁] [CommRing R₂] [CommRing S₁] [CommRing S₂]
    (f₁ : R₁ →+* S₁) (f₂ : R₂ →+* S₂) (x₁ : S₁) (x₂ : S₂) :
    (RingHom.prodMap f₁ f₂).IsIntegralElem (x₁, x₂) ↔
      f₁.IsIntegralElem x₁ ∧ f₂.IsIntegralElem x₂ := by
  let g₁ : (R₁ × R₂) →+* S₁ := f₁.comp (RingHom.fst R₁ R₂)
  let g₂ : (R₁ × R₂) →+* S₂ := f₂.comp (RingHom.snd R₁ R₂)
  letI : Algebra (R₁ × R₂) S₁ := g₁.toAlgebra
  letI : Algebra (R₁ × R₂) S₂ := g₂.toAlgebra
  have halg : algebraMap (R₁ × R₂) (S₁ × S₂) = RingHom.prod g₁ g₂ := by
    ext r <;> rfl
  have hpair :
      (RingHom.prod g₁ g₂).IsIntegralElem (x₁, x₂) ↔
        g₁.IsIntegralElem x₁ ∧ g₂.IsIntegralElem x₂ := by
    rw [← halg]
    exact IsIntegral.pair_iff
  have hfst : Function.Surjective (RingHom.fst R₁ R₂) := by
    intro r
    exact ⟨(r, 0), rfl⟩
  have hsnd : Function.Surjective (RingHom.snd R₁ R₂) := by
    intro r
    exact ⟨(0, r), rfl⟩
  have h₁ : g₁.IsIntegralElem x₁ ↔ f₁.IsIntegralElem x₁ := by
    exact integralElem_comp_surjective_iff (RingHom.fst R₁ R₂) hfst f₁
  have h₂ : g₂.IsIntegralElem x₂ ↔ f₂.IsIntegralElem x₂ := by
    exact integralElem_comp_surjective_iff (RingHom.snd R₁ R₂) hsnd f₂
  rw [show f₁.prodMap f₂ = RingHom.prod g₁ g₂ by ext r <;> rfl, hpair, h₁, h₂]

end StacksPart01

data.content:
- A rejected proof attempt is evidence, not a commit. Before deleting or replacing
  a substantial draft, preserve it with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" attempt save <files...> --reason "why it failed"`
  (optionally `--diagnostics <file>`). The dashboard reports the artifact
  separately from durable commits, so the next session can inspect the dead end
  without restoring it to the working tree.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

For source-backed formalization, add a compact epistemic checkpoint to the same
report (it is not needed for an ordinary tooling task):
`Claim class: proved producer | conditional interface | imported boundary |
empty/vacuous | axiom/sorry-backed | unverified`; `Frontier before/after:` the
source-facing node and first unmet producer; `Consumer:` the intended downstream
declaration/node; and `Evidence:` the exact target/build, transitive `#print axioms`,
and source/graph status. State `honesty-reviewer: used` or `skipped — <reason>`
when a certificate, completion claim, or repeated frontier triggered the lane.
A conditional or imported class may be a useful handoff, but it must not be
described as discharging the source theorem or justify a source-facing `\leanok`.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is an available fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy benefits from an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — progress-integrity review of one task; is the claimed work
  real, task-scoped, and converging rather than looping?
- **honesty-reviewer** — anti-evasion review of certificates, completion claims,
  hidden assumptions, vacuity, and repeated unchanged frontiers.
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

      "body": "AN 'ONLY PRODUCER IS FIELD-ONLY' CLAIM IS A CENSUS OF THE NAME YOU GUESSED, AND THE RING-LEVEL VERSION IS OFTEN LANDED UNDER A DIFFERENT MAP.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g 0096 r6, refuted by a fresh-context audit of my own file). I published that the picEtAffineEquiv/unit presentation seam has exactly one general producer -- PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section -- that it is stated over a FIELD and needs a curve section there, and that ring-level surjectivity of PicEtAff.unit is therefore the honest next brick. Every clause was checkable and the conclusion was false: picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:161) supplies the same seam at an ARBITRARY test RING, no field, no section, no curve binder, with 11 call sites.\n\nWHY MY CENSUS MISSED IT, and this is the reusable part. I searched for producers of the SEAM'S NAME -- surjectivity of  -- because that is the shape of the conclusion I wanted. The landed producer is not about 's surjectivity at all: it is an AFFINE-CONSISTENCY lemma for a DIFFERENT map (relPicToPicEt) which happens to have the seam as its conclusion. A grep for 'unit_surjective' finds it never; a search for the CONCLUSION 'picEtAffineEquiv _ = PicEtAff.unit _ _' finds it first.\n\nSO THE RULE: when you are about to write 'the only producer is X, and X is too strong', search for the CONCLUSION you need, not for the strengthened statement whose name you have. The name census answers 'who proved this lemma'; the obligation is 'who lands this Prop', and a lemma about another map can land it while carrying none of the binders you were about to price.\n\nAND THE SECOND-ORDER COST, which is why this is worth a memory item rather than a header note: the false claim RELOCATED THE GAP. I named ring-level surjectivity of  as the next brick; the actually-open statement is surjectivity of relPicToPicEt onto picEt -- a different map, different proof, and one the tree already treats as a real condition (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199 calls membership in its range 'honesty'). A misidentified next brick sends the next lane to build something nobody needs.",

      "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it. The strengthening was FROM a weak condition my own file proved holds at the curve TO one my own project proved fails at the Picard scheme.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE RULE. When you replace a hypothesis H by a 'more standard' H', H' => H is not enough -- that direction is what makes the substitution LOOK conservative. Ask what H' implies that H does not (here: quasi-compactness), then check that consequence at the intended witness. And grep your own tree for a file whose title is a negation ('NotProper', 'NoGo', 'Refute') before publishing a strengthening: the counterexample is often already landed one import away.\n\nALSO: the weakened repair is where tautologies hide. My first repair -- 'every finite set that lies in a good open lies in an affine open' -- is PROVABLE for every scheme with its hypothesis unused. Elaborate the candidate weakening with the binder discarded before shipping it (pic-g filed the same shape as I-1660 the same day).",

      "body": "A LOCALISATION REDUCTION IS EMPTIED BY THE CONSUMER OWN OUTER QUANTIFIER, AND EVERY PER-STATEMENT CHECK PASSES.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, AJCR 0096 r7, Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean; audit I-1657/I-1660, reproduced by me).\n\nWHAT HAPPENED. I reduced an obligation P(A) at an arbitrary test algebra to a pointwise-local form: for every prime p of A, some f outside p with P(Localization.Away f). At a FIXED A that is a real reduction with no route back, and I verified it. I then composed it over all A into two producers of the goal object -- and those hypotheses are LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the global ones they were meant to weaken, because Localization.Away f is ITSELF a test algebra, so the consumer own forall-A already ranges over it. The converse is one line with the trivial witness f = 1.\n\nWHY EVERY CHECK PASSED. Sorry-free, axiom-clean against a sorryAx control, rooted, build green, non-vacuous (both hypotheses used, linter clean), and the fixed-A lemma genuinely is a reduction. Nothing local to any statement is wrong. The defect is the INTERACTION between my inner quantifier and the consumer outer one, and no per-statement check can see it.\n\nTHE TEST, and it costs one probe: before pricing a localisation, pointwise, or restriction reduction as progress, PROVE THE CONVERSE WITH THE TRIVIAL WITNESS -- f = 1, the identity localisation, V = top, the whole space. If it closes, the reduction only helps at a FIXED base object, and you must then check whether the consumer has that shape. Mine did not.\n\nSECOND, SMALLER TRAP FROM THE SAME FILE: my \"local ring\" interface was about Localization.Away f, which is a BASIC OPEN and not a local ring (IsLocalRing fails to synthesize). A lane with a genuinely local computation holds Localization.AtPrime, and the AtPrime-to-Away bridge is spreading out -- ask which one your consumer actually has before naming the interface.\n\nSibling of \"substitute the trivial value in layer one\" and \"free factor vs localisation\".",

      "body": "DUPLICATION, DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean: the headline \"the FIRST inhabitant of DivFamZar at ANY parameter\" is FALSE over a field, and the uniqueness proof re-derives what two landed quotient-level lemmas already give.\n\nINHABITATION WAS NOT FIRST. exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq (DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:143, the landed B-3 hsurj) at D = 0 gives a DivFam C K pi 0 with divFamDivisor = 0, hence DivFamZar C K pi 0 via toZar; divFamFieldEquiv.symm (0, le_rfl, by simp) gives the same class directly, and Quotient.out of it gives a CertifiedDivisorFamily C K pi 0. VERIFIED in a probe importing ONLY DivisorFamilyFieldSurj + DivSchemeAbel, no pic-c file, lake env lean EXIT=0. The correct claim is narrower and still worth having: trivZar is the first inhabitant at a GENERAL TEST RING R, where no field-surjectivity route applies.\n\nUNIQUENESS RE-DERIVES A LANDED LEMMA. presentationDivisor_eq_zero_of_isCertified_zero + divEq_of_isCertified_zero (:103, :114) work per-adaptation and then re-run divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq. But divFamDivisor_injective (DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv.lean:177) is exactly that step already packaged at the QUOTIENT level, and DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean imports DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv directly. With zero_le_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyField.lean:165) and deg_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:376), both also in closure, the whole file's math is:\n  hx : divFamDivisor x = 0 := eq_zero_of_deg_le_zero K (zero_le_divFamDivisor x) (deg rewrite; norm_num)\n  same for y; exact divFamDivisor_injective (hx.trans hy.symm)\nVERIFIED at the file's exact import list minus DivisorFamilyDegreeZero, EXIT=0. Two of the three declarations in the \"Main declarations\" list are avoidable, and the docstring's \"in one line each\" argument describes the longer of two routes without noting the shorter one exists.\n\nALSO: instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero and uniqueZeroOfField carry [LocallyOfFiniteType (relCurve C K over Spec K)] which is NOT load-bearing: it is inferInstance from the SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 binder two lines up (Smooth => LocallyOfFiniteType). Verified by re-elaborating both without it, EXIT=0.",

      "body": "TWO PROSE DEFECTS, DivisorFamilyDegreeZero.lean.\n\n(1) \"0 is the UNIQUE degree at which the rank clause is vacuous\" (:37-39, :216-218, plus the commit message and the roadmap summary) is false as stated. The clause is vacuous whenever PrimeSpectrum R is EMPTY, i.e. over the trivial ring, and there trivAdapt is certified at EVERY n. Verified: with R = ULift PUnit, all seven fields of IsCertified n close for every n (rankAtStalk_glued := fun p => (IsEmpty.false p).elim), giving DivFamZar C R pi n inhabited at arbitrary n. EXIT=0. The intended fact IS true and should be stated with its hypothesis: over a NONTRIVIAL R, trivAdapt satisfies six of the seven clauses at every n and fails rankAtStalk_glued at every n > 0 -- I verified that refutation too (Nontrivial R gives a prime, rankAtStalk of a subsingleton is 0, contradicting = 1). Correct version: \"over any nontrivial test ring, 0 is the unique degree at which trivAdapt's rank clause holds\".\n\n(2) A SECOND nonexistent cited name, in the same main-declarations list whose fabricated citation commit fc9dda7cbe was written to retract. Line 47-48 reads \"trivZar -- hence DivFamZar C R pi 0 is inhabited, and instInhabitedDivFamZarZero registers it.\" No such declaration exists anywhere in the tree; the instance at :245 is instNonemptyDivFamZarZero and gives Nonempty, not Inhabited. The retraction commit rewrote the list around the divFunctor_obj_nonempty_zero line and left this one, so the list a reader hits first still contains an ungreppable name -- the retraction paragraph now vouches for the very list it failed to check.\n\nMINOR, same family: DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean:69 cites CertifiedDivisorFamily.windowGen. It exists (DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel.lean:334) but is OUTSIDE that file's import closure, so #check fails there. Not fabricated, but not verifiable at the citing site either.",

      "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "id": "I-1530",

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

          "body": "RIDER, and it nearly caused a second bogus repair. Verify board prose by PARSING the summary field, never by grepping the file.\n\nAfter a roadmap set --pin-commit write I grepped for my newly appended section and got 0 hits, concluded the CLI had clobbered me again, and started re-appending. The grep was wrong, not the CLI: yaml.safe_dump wraps at 88 columns, so any phrase longer than a few words spans lines and no grep can match it. python3 -c \"yaml.safe_load(...)[\\\"summary\\\"]\" then showed all five distinctive phrases present, 14685 chars, three pins, owner cleared.\n\nSo the original rule (check the commit STAT) stands, and this is its companion: a zero grep hit on board prose is evidence about line wrapping, not about content. Both halves matter -- the stat catches real loss, and parsing prevents inventing loss that did not happen."

      "body": "VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.\n\nAJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:\n  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F\n  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)\n  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)\nEach docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.\n\nTHE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.",

      "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

name: hgraph
description: The dependency graph — Horizon's vendored hgraph core keeps one file per statement/Lean declaration under <project>/hgraph/; `horizon graph frontier` ranks work and agents attach node-scoped comments and reviews. This is the only DAG engine.
---

Each project may carry an **hgraph**: a plain-files semantic graph under
`<project>/hgraph/` — one Markdown node per blueprint statement and per Lean
declaration, typed edges (`uses` = the hard dependency DAG, `formalizes` =
informal↔formal identity). `horizon graph sync` (run automatically at run boundaries)
reconciles the blueprint + Lean sources into it; your **authored** additions
(comments, reviews, metadata) are never touched by sync. The files are
committed to the workspace ledger like everything else.

Use `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …`; when a workspace has one project,
`-p` is optional. Address nodes by `label:<latex-label>` or
`decl:<lean-fqname>` — raw ids are opaque hashes. Most commands accept `--json`.

## Sync it yourself — and act on the warnings

Don't wait for the run boundary: after you change blueprint statements,
`\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations, or Lean declarations, run
`"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> sync` and **read its output**. Sync prints warnings for exactly the defects
you can fix on the spot: `\uses{X} has no blueprint node` (missing/mistyped
label), `\lean{Name} not found in Lean sources` (renamed or unwritten
declaration), stale nodes whose source vanished. Fix what your change caused
before moving on; a warning you deliberately leave (e.g. a forward reference
you'll write next) gets a node comment or a memory item so the next session
knows it's intentional. Sync is idempotent and never touches your authored
comments/reviews/metadata.

## Read

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> list --state ready` — nodes whose dependencies are all closed:
  provable *now*. Other states: `closed`, `blocked`, `formalized_open`.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` — the ready nodes ranked by how many downstream nodes a
  proof would unlock. **Use this when picking the next node to prove.**
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:thm:foo` — one node: statement, `lean_status`
  (`lean_ok | mathlib_ok | sorry | empty`, derived from scanning the Lean, not
  from `\leanok`), deps, attached comments/reviews.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> ancestors label:thm:foo` — the dependency cone.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> stats` — per-state counts for the project.

## Write — per-node progress lives WITH the node

- **Comment = failure memory / progress note on that node.** When an approach
  fails or you learn something node-specific, record it where the next session
  will look first:
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add comment label:thm:foo --content "tried simp+ring, fails because …"`
  Agent authorship plus run/session/task provenance are filled from the run
  environment; do not copy the note into the blueprint.
- **Review = a Maths / Lean verdict** (independent axes, `good|bad`):
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add review label:thm:foo --maths good --lean bad --lean-comment "statement ok; proof has a sorry at the succ case"`
- **Metadata**: `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> modify node label:thm:foo --set status=verified`

Prefer node comments over inbox items for anything scoped to ONE node; use the
inbox (skill: `horizon-inbox`) for cross-node or cross-session coordination.

An edge `source --uses--> target` means *source depends on target*. A node is
"ready" when all of its dependencies are closed; prefer `frontier`, which ranks
ready nodes by what they unlock. The dashboard provides the workspace project
switcher and the chapter-collapsed Graphviz view.

## Relation to the blueprint

The DAG **is** the hgraph — there is no second engine and no parser fallback.
It is generated by resolving the blueprint's `\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations
against the real Lean sources, so keeping those annotations correct (skill:
`blueprint-conventions`) is exactly what keeps this graph correct. Unresolved
references surface as `horizon graph sync` warnings and as `dangling` entries — read
the warnings rather than trusting `dangling` alone.

def Pi.evalNonUnitalRingHom (f : I → Type v) [∀ i, NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring (f i)] (i : I) :
    (∀ i, f i) →ₙ+* f i :=
  { Pi.evalMulHom f i, Pi.evalAddMonoidHom f i with }

/-- `Function.const` as a `NonUnitalRingHom`. -/
@[simps]
def Pi.constNonUnitalRingHom (α β : Type*) [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring β] : β →ₙ+* α → β :=
  { NonUnitalRingHom.pi fun _ => NonUnitalRingHom.id β with toFun := Function.const _ }

/-- Non-unital ring homomorphism between the function spaces `I → α` and `I → β`, induced by a
non-unital ring homomorphism `f` between `α` and `β`. -/
@[simps]
protected def NonUnitalRingHom.compLeft {α β : Type*} [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring α]
    [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring β] (f : α →ₙ+* β) (I : Type*) : (I → α) →ₙ+* I → β :=
  { f.toMulHom.compLeft I, f.toAddMonoidHom.compLeft I with toFun := fun h => f ∘ h }

end NonUnitalRingHom

section RingHom

universe u v

variable {I : Type u}

/-- A family of ring homomorphisms `f a : γ →+* β a` defines a ring homomorphism
`RingHom.pi f : γ →+* Π a, β a` given by `RingHom.pi f x b = f b x`. -/
@[simps]
protected def RingHom.pi {f : I → Type*} {γ : Type*} [∀ i, NonAssocSemiring (f i)]
    [NonAssocSemiring γ] (g : ∀ i, γ →+* f i) : γ →+* ∀ i, f i :=
  { MonoidHom.pi fun i => (g i).toMonoidHom, AddMonoidHom.pi fun i => (g i).toAddMonoidHom with
    toFun := fun x b => g b x }

@[deprecated (since := "2026-05-30")] protected alias Pi.ringHom := RingHom.pi
@[deprecated (since := "2026-05-30")] protected alias Pi.ringHom_apply := RingHom.pi_apply

theorem RingHom.pi_injective {f : I → Type*} {γ : Type*} [Nonempty I] [∀ i, NonAssocSemiring (f i)]
    [NonAssocSemiring γ] (g : ∀ i, γ →+* f i) (hg : ∀ i, Function.Injective (g i)) :
    Function.Injective (RingHom.pi g) :=
  MonoidHom.pi_injective (fun i => (g i).toMonoidHom) hg

@[deprecated (since := "2026-05-30")] protected alias Pi.ringHom_injective := RingHom.pi_injective

/-- Evaluation of functions into an indexed collection of rings at a point is a ring
homomorphism. This is `Function.eval` as a `RingHom`. -/
@[simps!]
def Pi.evalRingHom (f : I → Type v) [∀ i, NonAssocSemiring (f i)] (i : I) : (∀ i, f i) →+* f i :=
  { Pi.evalMonoidHom f i, Pi.evalAddMonoidHom f i with }

instance (f : I → Type*) [∀ i, Semiring (f i)] (i) :
    RingHomSurjective (Pi.evalRingHom f i) where
  is_surjective x := ⟨by classical exact (if h : · = i then h ▸ x else 0), by simp⟩

/-- `Function.const` as a `RingHom`. -/
@[simps]
def Pi.constRingHom (α β : Type*) [NonAssocSemiring β] : β →+* α → β :=
  { RingHom.pi fun _ => RingHom.id β with toFun := Function.const _ }

/-- Ring homomorphism between the function spaces `I → α` and `I → β`, induced by a ring
homomorphism `f` between `α` and `β`. -/
@[simps]
protected def RingHom.compLeft {α β : Type*} [NonAssocSemiring α] [NonAssocSemiring β]
    (f : α →+* β) (I : Type*) : (I → α) →+* I → β :=
  { f.toMonoidHom.compLeft I, f.toAddMonoidHom.compLeft I with toFun := fun h => f ∘ h }

end RingHom

import Mathlib.RingTheory.IntegralClosure.IsIntegral.Basic
import Mathlib.RingTheory.IntegralClosure.IsIntegralClosure.Basic
import Mathlib.RingTheory.IntegralClosure.IntegrallyClosed

/-!
# Integral elements and towers

This file packages the element-level transport statements used throughout the
finite and integral extension sections of the Stacks Project.  The underlying
predicates are Mathlib's `RingHom.IsIntegralElem` and `IsIntegral`.
-/

namespace StacksPart01

/-! ### Transport of integral elements -/

/-- Integral elements remain integral after applying a ring homomorphism. -/
theorem integralElem_map
    {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [Ring S] [Ring T]
    (f : R →+* S) (g : S →+* T) {x : S}
    (hx : f.IsIntegralElem x) :
    (g.comp f).IsIntegralElem (g x) := by
  exact hx.map g

/-- Along an injective ring map, integrality of an image is equivalent to
integrality of the original element. -/
theorem integralElem_map_iff_of_injective
    {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [Ring S] [Ring T]
    (f : R →+* S) (g : S →+* T) (hg : Function.Injective g) {x : S} :
    (g.comp f).IsIntegralElem (g x) ↔ f.IsIntegralElem x := by
  exact RingHom.IsIntegralElem.map_iff hg

/-- If an element is integral for a composite map, it is integral for the
second map. -/
theorem integralElem_of_comp
    {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Ring T]
    (f : R →+* S) (g : S →+* T) {x : T}
    (hx : (g.comp f).IsIntegralElem x) :
    g.IsIntegralElem x := by
  exact RingHom.IsIntegralElem.of_comp hx

/-! ### Cancellation in towers -/

/-- If a composite ring map is integral, then its second factor is integral
(Stacks, Tag 02JM). -/
theorem ringHom_isIntegral_of_comp
    {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T]
    (f : R →+* S) (g : S →+* T)
    (h : (g.comp f).IsIntegral) : g.IsIntegral := by
  exact RingHom.IsIntegral.tower_top f g h

/-- If the second map is injective and a composite is integral, then the first
map is integral. -/
theorem ringHom_isIntegral_of_comp_injective
    {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T]
    (f : R →+* S) (g : S →+* T) (hg : Function.Injective g)
    (h : (g.comp f).IsIntegral) : f.IsIntegral := by
  exact RingHom.IsIntegral.tower_bot f g hg h

/-! ### Towers and integral closures -/

/-- Integrality is transitive in an algebra tower. -/
theorem isIntegral_tower
    {R A B : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Ring B]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R A]
    [IsScalarTower R A B] [Algebra.IsIntegral R A]
    (x : B) (hx : IsIntegral A x) : IsIntegral R x := by
  exact isIntegral_trans x hx

/-- For an injective algebra map, an element of the lower algebra is integral
over the base exactly when its image in the upper algebra is. -/
theorem isIntegral_algebraMap_iff_of_injective
    {R A B : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Ring B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsScalarTower R A B] (hAB : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    {x : A} :
    IsIntegral R ((algebraMap A B) x) ↔ IsIntegral R x := by
  exact isIntegral_algebraMap_iff hAB

/-- An integral element in an integrally closed extension comes from the base
ring. -/
theorem exists_algebraMap_eq_of_integral
    {R A : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [IsIntegrallyClosedIn R A] {x : A} (hx : IsIntegral R x) :
    ∃ y : R, algebraMap R A y = x := by
  exact IsIntegrallyClosedIn.algebraMap_eq_of_integral hx

/-! ### Integral closure and localization -/

/-- The integral closure commutes with localization (Stacks, Tag `0307`).

The `IsLocalization` conclusion records the canonical localized-ring model,
which is the type-correct Lean form of the source's equality of subrings. -/
theorem integralClosure_isLocalization
    {R S Rm Sm : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [CommRing Rm] [CommRing Sm] [Algebra R Rm] [Algebra S Sm]
    [Algebra Rm Sm] [Algebra R Sm] [IsScalarTower R S Sm]
    [IsScalarTower R Rm Sm] (M : Submonoid R)
    [IsLocalization M Rm]
    [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S M) Sm]
    [Algebra (integralClosure R S) (integralClosure Rm Sm)]
    [IsScalarTower (integralClosure R S) (integralClosure Rm Sm) Sm]
    [IsScalarTower R (integralClosure R S) (integralClosure Rm Sm)] :
    IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (integralClosure R S) M)
      (integralClosure Rm Sm) := by
  exact IsLocalization.integralClosure (S := S) (Rf := Rm) (Sf := Sm) M

/-- An element is integral over the base ring exactly when its image is
integral after localization at every prime of the base
(Stacks, Tag `034K`). -/
theorem isIntegral_iff_isIntegral_localizationAtPrime
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (x : S) :
    IsIntegral R x ↔ ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      IsIntegral (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
        (algebraMap S
          (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S p.asIdeal.primeCompl)) x) := by
  constructor
  · intro hx p
    obtain ⟨q, hq, hqx⟩ := hx
